newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar ends firm amid spec, local buying.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar ends firm amid spec, local buying.

text.p: CSCE world July sugar futures settled higher across the board despite a weakening of the July/October spread, market sources said.
Mixed trade and local buying triggered stops around 11.20 cents in the October contract and attracted fund buying, lifting the market to the day's high of 11.32 cents.
"People think the market is going up so we have three more days of fireworks," Merrill Lynch sugar broker Peter Perez, said, referring to the expiry of the July contract on Monday.
Open interest in the July contract fell by 2,183 lots to 28,775 lots.
The July/October spread closed at 0.11 cent October premium, compared with 0.07 cent on Tuesday's close.
The March, May and July 1998 contracts climbed to fresh, life-of-contract highs during the sessin.
Resistance in the most-active October contract was pegged at 11.34 cents, just above today's high, followed by 11.42 cents.
The July contract closed 0.07 cent higher at 11.15 cents per lb, traded 11.16 to 11.00 cents. October settled up 0.11 cent at 11.26 cents, while the rest of the board ended 0.10 to 0.12 higher.
Support in October was pegged at 11.00 cents and then at the recent low of 10.96 cents in October, where sell stops could trigger a speculative-driven selloff, traders said.
An estimated 39,618 lots changed hands on the day, compared with Tuesday's official 25,066 lots.
